en: A pulley changes the direction of the applied force, making it easier to lift a heavy bucket of water from a well.
Brake pads press against a bicycle wheel's metal rim, creating friction that converts kinetic energy into heat to stop the bike.
The Moon's gravitational pull on Earth's oceans causes the water to bulge, creating high and low tides every day.
Wrapping a copper wire around an iron nail and connecting it to a battery creates an electromagnet that picks up paperclips.
Closing a switch completes an electrical circuit, allowing electrons to flow through a tungsten filament and produce light in a bulb.
Light waves bend when they pass from air into water, making a pencil partially submerged in a glass look broken.
Striking a drum skin makes it vibrate, which pushes nearby air molecules to create sound waves that travel to your ear.
Placing a metal spoon in hot soup transfers thermal energy from the liquid to the handle through direct particle collisions.
Stretching a rubber band stores elastic potential energy, which transforms into kinetic energy when released to shoot a paper ball.
An axe acts as a wedge by concentrating the force of a swing into a thin edge to split firewood apart.
Pushing the north pole of one bar magnet toward the north pole of another creates a repulsive force that pushes them apart.
Rubbing a balloon on hair transfers electrons to the balloon, giving it a negative charge that attracts neutral pieces of paper.
